subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a public delayed/batch agent-turn lifecycle, and should the first supported caller be isolated cron jobs only or a broader shared background-turn contract?
rationale: Provider batch APIs are asynchronous and provider-specific, while the requested behavior crosses public Plugin SDK, protocol, state, delivery, cancellation, accounting, and authentication boundaries; code review cannot safely choose those permanent contracts.

options.title: Cron-first delayed-turn contract
options.body: Define an additive SDK/runtime lifecycle and initially expose it only for isolated cron agentTurn jobs, with explicit completion, cancellation, delivery, and provider-eligibility semantics.

options.title: Shared background-turn contract
options.body: Design one broader delayed-turn API for cron, sessions, subagents, and heartbeat callers before shipping any provider implementation.

options.title: Keep external for now
options.body: Defer core support and document external provider batch workflows until a stable OpenClaw lifecycle contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Cron-first delayed-turn contract
recommendation.body: Define an additive SDK/runtime lifecycle and initially expose it only for isolated cron agentTurn jobs, with explicit completion, cancellation, delivery, and provider-eligibility semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and the latest substantive review connect this person most directly to the provider/runtime and cron decision surface.
